shared/home-intro.html.code:
Hello, Everyone

I’m a product designer and design lead. I turn complex workflows and business requirements into clear, usable B2B and B2C products, from early discovery through launch and ongoing improvement.

I enjoy the stage when the problem is still taking shape: making sense of complexity and helping a team find a clear direction. My work combines hands-on design, research, and team leadership, with close attention to the small details people encounter every day.

shared/about-main.html.code:
I’m Dima, a designer with a background in banking, classifieds, and marketplaces. I’ve worked with companies and brands including Yandex, Raiffeisen Bank, Decathlon, and Leroy Merlin, as well as small teams and startups. My projects span Russia, Cyprus, and the US.

I like small changes that make products easier to use. There’s often a lot of thought and teamwork behind something that looks simple. I stay hands-on while shaping how design teams work.

How I work

To clarify our goals and explore how to reach them, I discuss ideas with stakeholders, review data, and talk to users. I care about how an interface works, looks, and feels — and its impact on the business.

Having built websites myself, I’m comfortable reading code and discussing technical decisions with engineers. I also build workflows with AI agents to support design and research.

I enjoy helping designers see their strengths and decide where to grow. Competency frameworks and individual development plans help us agree on next steps.

Outside of work

In my triathlon days, I ran several marathons, completed a half Ironman, and logged thousands of kilometers on Zwift. I also started a local running club.

I enjoy skiing and cycling. When I want some time to myself, I head out on my paddleboard — I love the quiet out on the water.

Dmitry Rybalka
Home About Work Email LinkedIn Resume Telegram
Back

About me

I’m Dima, a designer with a background in banking, classifieds, and marketplaces. I’ve worked with companies and brands including Yandex, Raiffeisen Bank, Decathlon, and Leroy Merlin, as well as small teams and startups. My projects span Russia, Cyprus, and the US.

I like small changes that make products easier to use. There’s often a lot of thought and teamwork behind something that looks simple. I stay hands-on while shaping how design teams work.

How I work

To clarify our goals and explore how to reach them, I discuss ideas with stakeholders, review data, and talk to users. I care about how an interface works, looks, and feels — and its impact on the business.

Having built websites myself, I’m comfortable reading code and discussing technical decisions with engineers. I also build workflows with AI agents to support design and research.

I enjoy helping designers see their strengths and decide where to grow. Competency frameworks and individual development plans help us agree on next steps.

Outside of work

In my triathlon days, I ran several marathons, completed a half Ironman, and logged thousands of kilometers on Zwift. I also started a local running club.

I enjoy skiing and cycling. When I want some time to myself, I head out on my paddleboard — I love the quiet out on the water.

Let’s Talk

in mind? Drop me a message — or just say hello!

renderArticlePage validates unique document IDs and local accessibility/SVG targets before returning HTML. Conflicting explicit section IDs fail with a clear error.

shared/reading-page.html is the local full-document shell used by renderArticlePage. It includes the existing analytics head; the source viewer exposes the component markup and setup files rather than duplicating analytics bootstraps.

shared/site-controls.js compiles to /assets/site-controls.js on reading pages and DS. HOME embeds the same code inside app.js at its approved startup point. Define window.mobileLayout with the current layout media query before using these handlers.

renderComponent returns the current About page regions. To create a full page from confirmed content, use renderArticlePage({title, canonical, intro, sections, ...}) from the same library. It returns HTML and does not create a file or publish it.

Register an article route, exact files, consumers and canonical JSON contentSource once in shared/site-pages.mjs; the existing build handles document generation, usage stamps, fingerprints and publication validation. Keep /about/about.css and /about/about.js for the one-time reading entrance, native footer overlap and reduced-motion/focus handling. No Figma file is needed to reuse this existing composition.
